chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

My father (peace be upon him) would call for the ablution while traveling, and he was in his mount. Then a water-skin was brought to him containing water, so he performed ablution, then he prayed the eight [rak'at] and the witr while in his mount. And when he dismounted, he prayed the two [rak'at] and the Fajr prayer.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams perform ablution and prayer while traveling on their mounts?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical flexibility (rukhas) granted to travelers, illustrating how Imam al-Sadiq (AS) maintained spiritual discipline by performing ablution and prayer while mounted in his saddle. It specifically distinguishes between the voluntary night prayers (eight rak'at and Witr) performed in transit and the obligatory Fajr prayer, which he reserved for when he dismounted, reflecting the scholarly principle of adapting worship to the constraints of travel without compromising its essence.
